cases.evidence: Boundary split 'Avenger class' from its head; first two pieces mistranslated as separate vessel types.
cases.proposed_rule: Demote any candidate boundary that splits a CapitalizedWord + 'class' sequence from the following noun (pattern: /[A-Z][a-z]+\s+class/); treat it as a last-resort cut only if no safer cuts exist.

example_pair.input: An Avenger class mine countermeasures ship, the ship was on its way to Puerto Princesa in Palawan.
example_pair.output: An Avenger class mine countermeasures ship<SEG:1>, the ship was on its way to Puerto Princesa in Palawan.

cases.evidence: Boundary before parenthetical led to wrong transliteration ('Daesh' → 'ダッシュ') because clarifying acronym wasn't visible.
cases.proposed_rule: Forbid a boundary between a named token and an immediately following parenthetical/parenthesized acronym/alternate name: if '(' appears within 1 token after a capitalized or unknown name token, keep the name+parenthetical uncut.

example_pair.input: Police said they suspect an alleged Daesh (ISIL) militant of responsibility for the attack.
example_pair.output: Police said they suspect an alleged Daesh (ISIL) militant of responsibility for the attack.<SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Segment ended after 'Carrying' and was translated as carrying people rather than carrying others' bags (patient unresolved).
cases.proposed_rule: Do not place a boundary after a gerund (-ing) when it is followed within 1–3 tokens by a prepositional phrase beginning with 'for','of', or 'to' (pattern: V-ing + (for|of|to) ...); keep them together.

example_pair.input: Carrying for others - Never let your bags out of your sight, especially when you are crossing international borders.
example_pair.output: Carrying for others -<SEG:1> Never let your bags out of your sight, especially when you are crossing international borders.

cases.evidence: Boundary separated 'remove' and pronoun 'it', causing the verb to be translated without its object and yield nonsense.
cases.proposed_rule: Forbid boundaries between an infinitival 'to' + verb and an immediately following pronoun or noun object (pattern: 'to' + Verb + Pronoun/Noun within 1 token); keep verb and its object together.

example_pair.input: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.
example_pair.output: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin<SEG:1> will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

cases.evidence: Segment ended after a four-digit year and the date was prematurely converted into an era name in Japanese.
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid boundaries that isolate a four-digit year (\d{4}) when it is followed or preceded by commas and a person name or clause; keep the year with the following clause to prevent premature era conversion.

example_pair.input: On September 24, 1759, Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000 year lease for the St James' Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland.
example_pair.output: On September 24, 1759, Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000 year lease for the St James' Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland.<SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Boundary after 'for how many' caused the translator to produce unrelated content rather than wait for the noun/clause head.
cases.proposed_rule: Never segment between clause-introducing 'how'/'how many' (or fixed strings 'for how many') and the following noun phrase or clause head; delay until the noun/verb head appears.

example_pair.input: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi.
example_pair.output: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi.<SEG:1>

summary: The prompt still lets or ranks too-high boundaries that separate modifiers/labels from their head nouns, verbs from their objects, and named entities from immediate parentheticals — often because the cut sits just after a comma or a short modifier phrase. Fixes should focus on priority demotions or outright forbids for cuts that split (1) Capitalized-model + classifier sequences, (2) name + parenthetical acronym spans, (3) gerund + short prepositional complements, and (4) 'to' + verb + immediate pronoun objects, plus delaying cuts after clause introducers like 'for how many'.

aggregate.dominant_basis: No corpus rate identifies a dominant failure. Read the cases and `judge_distribution` for WHICH mechanism to fix — do not infer a rate from `case_label_counts`, those cases were selected for being the worst.

coverage.of: all sentences scored — a true corpus rate
coverage.meaning: sentences where the tightest budget asked for boundaries the prompt never marked, so pieces are missing outright

premature_among_judged.of: boundaries judged this iteration, selected as the WORST by measured contradiction — NOT a corpus rate, do not compare it against `coverage`

case_label_counts.of: the selected worst cases — NOT a rate
